gap: No controlled comparison varies both the base retriever and the form of the temporal signal: each published temporal-retrieval system hard-codes one temporal mechanism inside one pipeline (exponential decay inside a fixed three-signal hybrid; learnable decay inside graph-based retrieval; a hard as-of boundary inside a multimodal verifier), and the temporal pathologies are asserted to be architecture-agnostic without a transfer measurement. It is therefore unknown whether temporal re-ranking gains persist across BM25, dense and hybrid retrievers, and whether graded recency decay or valid-time membership is the appropriate signal for amended normative text.

evidence.quote: We propose a three-signal hybrid framework integrating BM25 lexical matching, dense semantic embeddings, and exponential temporal decay, which achieves 99.8% temporal accuracy and 50.8% entity precision across all three languages
Layer 2 integrates learnable exponential decay functions into graph-based retrieval
BM25 outperforms hybrid on multihop queries (ROUGE-L 0.304 vs. 0.239)

why_unaddressed: The three closest systems each integrate temporal handling into one architecture, and the legal framework paper that calls the pathologies architecture-agnostic reports no empirical comparison. The only retrieved regulatory comparison of sparse/dense/hybrid shows hybrid is not uniformly best (BM25 wins on multihop), which indicates base-retriever choice matters but was not tested with a temporal component.
research_question: How do the gains from temporal re-ranking over amended normative text vary across base retrievers (BM25, dense, hybrid) and temporal signal forms (none, recency decay, valid-time membership), and does any form dominate consistently?
potential_experiment: A factorial evaluation on a single held-out query set: base retriever in {BM25, dense, hybrid RRF} x temporal signal in {none, recency decay, valid-time gating, valid-time gating + semantic re-rank}, with matched retrieval depth and reader, reporting temporal contamination, nDCG/recall and answer accuracy per cell, plus a recency-only baseline and a hard as-of baseline.
verification_required: Confirm by citation/full-text inspection that none of the closest systems reports a cross-retriever transfer study (the two closest were abstract-only here), and re-check recent literature once the search budget allows.
